in_hebrew.name: יוואכים
in_hebrew.meaning: הוא שקבע אלוהים או שאלוהים יקים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם יוואכים הוא שילוב של שני מילים עבריות: 'יו' שפירושו 'אלוהים' ו'אקים' שפירושו 'יקים' או 'יקבע'. השם מופיע בתנ'ך כהשם של אביו של המלכה יוכבד, אולם לא בצורה זו. יוואכים הוא השם המשמש בקרב הנוצרים לתיאור הוריו של ישוע, יוסף ומריה, לפי מסורת הנוצרים.

in_greek.name: Ιωακείμ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Ιωακείμ είναι σύνθετο όνομα από το 'Ιω' που σημαίνει 'Θεός' και το 'ακείμ' που σημαίνει 'καταστήσει' ή 'αναστήσει'. Το όνομα αναφέρεται στον πατέρα της Παναγίας, σύμφωνα με την παράδοση της Ανατολικής Ορθόδοξης Εκκλησίας και της Ρωμαιοκαθολικής Εκκλησίας.

in_latin.name: Ioakim
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Ioakim ex duobus vocabulis hebraicis componitur: 'Io' quod est 'Deus' et 'akim' quod est 'constituat' vel 'suscitabit'. Nomen Ioakim in traditione christiana refertur ad patrem beatae Mariae Virginis et parentem Jesu Christi secundum carnem.

in_english.name: Joakim
in_english.meaning: God will establish or God will raise
in_english.long_meaning: The name Joakim is derived from the Hebrew name 'Yvoakim', which means 'God will establish' or 'God will raise'. The name is composed of two elements: 'Yo' meaning 'God' and 'akim' meaning 'to establish' or 'to raise'. In Christian tradition, Joakim is recognized as the father of the Virgin Mary and the paternal grandfather of Jesus Christ. The name has been used in various forms across different cultures and languages, reflecting its biblical and spiritual significance.

In the New Testament, there is a mention of a man named Joachim, who was the estranged husband of St. Anne, the mother of the Virgin Mary. This suggests that Joakim was a devout and pious man in biblical times, and his name may have been given to children as a mark of respect and admiration for the biblical character.

seo.title: Joakim: Meaning, Origin, and Significance in Christianity
seo.meta_description: Discover the meaning, origin, and significance of the Hebrew name Joakim in Christianity. Learn about its cultural and religious usage and its appeal.
seo.description_paragraph:
The name Joakim is a variation of the Hebrew name Yaakov, which means ‘God will raise up’. In Christianity, the name Joakim is often associated with the biblical figure of Joachim, the father of Saint Anne, the mother of the Virgin Mary. The name has a rich history and cultural significance, and is still popular among Christians today.

Joakim is derived from the Hebrew name Yaakov, which is one of the most common names in the Bible. The name Yaakov means ‘he who supplants’ or ‘he who follows after’, and is often associated with the idea of God’s provision and protection. The prefix ‘Yo’ in Joakim means ‘God will add’ or ‘God will raise up’, which gives the name a sense of divine blessing and support.

The name Joakim has a rich history in Christianity. In the apocryphal Gospel of James, Joachim is described as a pious and childless man who was visited by an angel, who told him that he would have a son. Joachim’s wife, Anna, also barren, was visited by the same angel and was told that she would bear a son. The couple’s son, named James, went on to become the first bishop of Jerusalem and is considered a saint in the Catholic and Orthodox churches.

Today, the name Joakim is still popular among Christians, particularly among those who value its rich history and cultural significance. The name has a strong biblical connection and is often used as a name for boys in Christian families. It is also a popular choice for boys in countries with strong Christian traditions, such as the Philippines and Mexico.
